request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

text:
The diagnosis sections are withheld, so the record does not state the condition. The best inference is gallbladder disease, since the procedure was a laparoscopic cholecystectomy and the discharge advice is about gallbladder disease and a low-fat diet. That points to chapter XI, K80 (cholelithiasis), but the exact condition is not documented.

A coder would normally query the clinician here rather than assign a diagnosis from the procedure alone. The procedure does not establish the diagnosis. Cholecystitis (K81) or a gallbladder polyp (K82) are also possible. Cholelithiasis is the most common indication for this operation, and the advice to avoid fatty foods "to prevent recurrence of symptoms" fits gallstone disease best. I am giving K80 as a provisional code, to be confirmed by a query or the full record.

CODE: K80
